objective: Summarize the Agent Skills open standard (the SKILL.md format) precisely enough to write a repository skill that teaches how to author standard-conformant skills, with sources.
scope: Sources: the Agent Skills specification and docs (agentskills.io: the specification page, what-are-skills, integrate-skills, and the best-practices or authoring pages if any), the reference repository (github.com/agentskills/agentskills, including skills-ref validation rules), and Anthropic's skill authoring best practices page (platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices) for complementary guidance. Fetch with your web tools (for example the Exa fetch tool).

Cover: directory layout; SKILL.md frontmatter fields with their exact constraints (name: allowed characters, length, matching the directory; description: length and what it must say; optional fields such as license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools); body content guidance and size limits; progressive disclosure (metadata, instructions, resources) and the optional scripts/, references/, assets/ directories; how file references should be written (relative paths, depth); validation (skills-ref validate); and any guidance about portability across agents and models. Quote exact limits.
constraints: Sourced facts only, with URL and section per point; label inference. The summary is the deliverable and may run to 1500 words.

criteria.text: Spec coverage: layout, every frontmatter field with exact constraints, body guidance, progressive disclosure, optional directories, file references and validation are each covered with a source

result:
result: Agent Skills spec summarized below. Note: the brief is about skill authoring, not the user's MCP-server-count question. This report does not answer that question, and nothing I read covers holyagent's 0.3.0 MCP servers.

**Sources and versions**
- S1: https://agentskills.io/specification. Fetched 2026-11-07, undated page.
- S2: https://agentskills.io/what-are-skills.
- S3: https://agentskills.io/integrate-skills.
- S4: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentskills/agentskills/main/skills-ref/src/skills_ref/validator.py and `skills-ref/README.md`, `main` branch, fetched 2026-11-07.
- S5: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices. The fetch was truncated after the "Advanced: executable code" section, so the checklist and runtime-environment sections were not read.
- I did not find a separate authoring or best-practices page on agentskills.io. I did not read `llms.txt`, so one may exist.

**Directory layout** (S1 "Directory structure"; S2)
- A skill is a directory containing at minimum `SKILL.md`.
- Optional: `scripts/`, `references/`, `assets/`, and "any additional files or directories".
- The file must be named exactly `SKILL.md` (S3 Step 1, "What to scan for").
- S3: the spec does not mandate where skill directories live. `.agents/skills/` is a widely adopted cross-client convention. Some clients also scan `.claude/skills/`.

**Frontmatter** (S1 "Frontmatter"; the file is YAML frontmatter between `---` lines, then Markdown)

| Field | Required | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | yes | 1-64 characters. Unicode lowercase alphanumerics (`a-z`, `0-9`) and `-` only. No leading or trailing hyphen. No `--`. Must match the parent directory name. |
| `description` | yes | 1-1024 characters, non-empty. Should say what the skill does and when to use it, with specific keywords. |
| `license` | no | A license name or a bundled license file name. Keep it short. |
| `compatibility` | no | 1-500 characters. Only for specific environment requirements (product, system packages, network). "Most skills do not need" it. |
| `metadata` | no | A map of string keys to string values. Use reasonably unique key names. |
| `allowed-tools` | no | A space-separated string of pre-approved tools, for example `Bash(git:*) Bash(jq:*) Read`. Marked Experimental; support varies by agent. |

- Good description (S1): "Extracts text and tables from PDF files, fills PDF forms, and merges multiple PDFs. Use when working with PDF documents or when the user mentions PDFs, forms, or document extraction."
- Poor description (S1): "Helps with PDFs."

**Anthropic-specific extras** (S5 "Skill structure"; these go beyond the open spec)
- `name` and `description` cannot contain XML tags.
- `name` cannot contain the reserved words `anthropic` or `claude`.
- Write the description in third person. It is injected into the system prompt, and "I can help you…" or "You can use this…" cause discovery problems.
- Prefer gerund names such as `processing-pdfs`. Noun phrases (`pdf-processing`) and verb phrases (`process-pdfs`) are acceptable.
- Avoid vague names (`helper`, `utils`) and generic ones (`documents`, `data`).

**Body** (S1 "Body content")
- "No format restrictions."
- Recommended sections: step-by-step instructions, input/output examples, common edge cases.
- The whole file is loaded on activation, so split longer content into referenced files.
- Size limits: keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines (S1; S5 repeats it) and under 5000 tokens (S1; S3 says "recommended").
- Content guidance (S5):
  - Be concise and only add context the model lacks.
  - Match specificity to how fragile the task is: high, medium or low freedom.
  - Offer a default instead of many options.
  - Avoid time-sensitive information; use an "old patterns" section.
  - Use consistent terminology.
  - Use checklists and validate-then-fix loops for complex workflows.
  - Include input/output examples.
  - Build evaluations first and iterate against observed behavior.

**Progressive disclosure** (S1; S2 "How do Agent Skills work"; S3 table)
1. Metadata (name and description) is loaded at startup. S1 says ~100 tokens; S3 says ~50-100 tokens per skill.
2. The `SKILL.md` body is loaded on activation, under 5000 tokens recommended.
3. Resources in `scripts/`, `references/` and `assets/` are loaded only when needed.

**Optional directories** (S1; these are recommendations, not requirements)
- `scripts/`: executable code that is self-contained or documents its dependencies, gives helpful error messages and handles edge cases. Languages depend on the agent; Python, Bash and JavaScript are common.
- `references/`: for example `REFERENCE.md`, `FORMS.md`, or domain files such as `finance.md`. Keep each file focused, because smaller files use less context.
- `assets/`: templates, images, data files.
- S5 adds: scripts should handle errors rather than defer to the model, and constants should be documented rather than left as unexplained values.

**File references** (S1 "File references"; S5)
- Use relative paths from the skill root, for example `[the reference guide](references/REFERENCE.md)` or `scripts/extract.py`.
- Keep references one level deep from `SKILL.md`. Avoid chains.
- S5 reason: the model may preview nested files with `head -100` and read them incompletely.
- S5: give reference files longer than 100 lines a table of contents.
- S5: always use forward slashes, even on Windows.

**Validation** (S1 "Validation"; S4)
- Command: `skills-ref validate ./my-skill`.
- S4 `validator.py` checks:
  - The path exists and is a directory, and `SKILL.md` exists.
  - The frontmatter parses.
  - Only these keys are allowed: `name`, `description`, `license`, `allowed-tools`, `metadata`, `compatibility`. Any other key is an error.
  - `name` and `description` are present and non-empty.
  - `name` is at most 64 characters (after NFKC normalization), lowercase, has no leading or trailing hyphen, has no `--`, uses only `isalnum()` characters or `-`, and equals the directory name.
  - `description` is at most 1024 characters.
  - `compatibility` is a string of at most 500 characters.
- Gaps in the validator (inference from the code): it does not check `metadata` value types, `allowed-tools` format, `license`, body length, or XML tags or reserved words.
- The validator's `isalnum()` accepts any Unicode letter, which is looser than the spec's wording of `a-z` and `0-9`.
- The README says the library is "for demonstration purposes only" and not for production. It also offers `read-properties` and `to-prompt`, which generates the `<available_skills>` XML.

**Portability** (S3; S5)
- The spec mandates no location. Cross-client discovery relies on the `.agents/skills/` convention (S3).
- Clients may be lenient: S3 warns but still loads on a name/directory mismatch or a name over 64 characters, and skips on a missing description or unparseable YAML. Authors should still follow the strict spec.
- S3: an unquoted colon in a value, such as `description: Use when: x`, is technically invalid YAML. Quote such values to be safe.
- S3: project-level skills override user-level ones on a name collision.
- S3: project skills from untrusted repos may be gated by a trust check.
- `allowed-tools` varies by client (S1).
- S5: test with every model you will use. Haiku may need more detail, and Opus may need less over-explanation.
- Inference: a portable skill should use only the six spec fields. Anthropic-only constraints are harmless to follow, but `disable-model-invocation` appears in S3 only as an example client flag, not as a spec field.

blockers: none
questions: The brief does not match the user's request (the count of MCP servers shipped in holyagent 0.3.0). Confirm this is the intended assignment, and say where the 0.3.0 plan lives if the count is still wanted.
notes: S5 was truncated, so check its "Checklist for effective Skills" section before finalizing. The `skills-ref` README and S3 describe the XML prompt format only as a recommendation.

evidence:
Spec coverage: the layout, all six frontmatter fields with exact limits, body guidance, progressive disclosure, optional directories, file references and validation are each covered above with an S1-S5 citation. S1 is https://agentskills.io/specification and S4 is the skills-ref `validator.py`.
